key_insight: Deep-learning emulators can reproduce a complex marine biogeochemistry model accurately across both short-term forecasts and multi-decadal projections, with improved skill over the parent model in some cases.
engineering_relevance: These emulators could enable much cheaper and faster operational ocean forecasting and climate-scale simulations while preserving key ecosystem dynamics.
method: LSTM networks emulate a selected subset of daily variables in the water column.
Physics-informed 1D CNNs emulate the full pelagic system throughout the water column at daily resolution.
Models are driven by ocean physics simulator inputs and tested for stability, decadal projections, and 10-day forecasts.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation against the parent model using daily variability, extreme events, forecast skill scores, and multi-decadal stability, including prediction of spring bloom timing years ahead.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated in a simplified one-dimensional water-column setup, so generalization to full three-dimensional regional ocean models remains unproven.
paper_title: Deep learning model emulators for marine biogeochemistry forecasting from days to decades
